basis: The firm filed Makena Capital Management under its own 'Investment Partnerships' category on every listing (2008 to 2016), and its page describes Makena as an investment management firm run by the team that ran the Stanford endowment: the position is a partnership interest in a fund manager, not equity in a venture-outcome operating company (decisions D6, T5, the LP-stake class)

note: SHV entered at the $25M Series B of June 2015, which it led as a new investor (SecurityWeek, 2015-06-08; Stefan Dyckerhoff joined the board); the $10.5M Series A of November 2014 came before it, so the entry reads Growth. Last priced mark: the $100M Series E led by Vista Equity Partners in November 2020 at an $800M enterprise valuation (FinTech Global), older than 24 months, so stale; no later priced round found. Still independent: it bought Votiro in February 2025 and named Bill Robbins CEO in February 2026. City aligned with General Catalyst's row (Mountain View); the firm's 2017 page said Menlo Park.

SHV and Investor Growth Capital led Ruckus's $9M second round, announced September 19, 2005, which existing investors Sequoia and WK Technology Fund completed (Wikipedia). The October 2012 S-1/A names that round Series C (7,835,000 shares at $1.15, $8.96M), after the Series A-1 seed ($1.5M from Sequoia and private investors) and the $3.5M Series B led by WK Technology Fund, so the entry reads Growth. Brocade bought Ruckus in May 2016 for about $1.5B; last HQ Sunnyvale; aligned with Sequoia's row (acquired, below_1b).

note: SHV entered at the $12M Series B of September 18, 2006, which it co-led with Split Rock Partners (the release on Split Rock's site). The first round, $8M in March 2006, was led by Trinity Ventures with REIT backers and does not name SHV (VentureBeat); Wikipedia's 'initially backed by' line merges the two rounds. RealPage bought the company (Multifamily Technology Solutions, d/b/a MyNewPlace, San Francisco) for about $74.4M in August 2011 (RealPage 8-K). Preferred ladder in RealPage's 8-K/A: Series A $8M, Series B $12M, B-1 $3.57M (2008 to 2009), B-2 $5M (December 2010).

note: Paragon Management Systems, Inc. is Adexa: formed in California in 1994 as successor to NP Complete and later renamed Adexa (supply chain planning software; FreeMarkets' 2001 S-4). The S-4 shows SHV funds holding 1,978,906 Series A shares (about half of the Series A, financed in 1997) plus Series B (1998, $3.30 a share) and Series C (August 2000, about $20M) shares, 18.0% of the company, with William Younger (SHV) a director, so the entry is the 1997 Series A. Adexa stayed independent after FreeMarkets' 2001 merger agreement and was acquired by Eyelit Technologies in January 2025 (Business Wire: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250114233508/en/Eyelit-Technologies-Acquires-Adexa-to-Expand-Smart-Factory-and-Supply-Chain-Solutions). HQ in the S-4: 5933 W. Century Blvd, Los Angeles. The published name could read Adexa.

TeleCommunication Systems bought the company (Aliso Viejo, CA) for $170M in cash, stock and notes, agreed 2009-12-01 (TCS 8-K); SHV received 232,731 TCS shares for its stake and James White (SHV) sat on the board until the sale (TCS S-3, February 2010). The first venture money was the $6.5M Series B of late 2004 (closings in September and December 2004), and the $10M Series C of 2006 was led by Mission Ventures (Orange County Business Journal; ladder in TCS's 8-K/A: Series A $250K in 2001, A-1 $1.03M in 2003). SHV is named only among the venture investors, so it entered at the 2004 Series B or the 2006 Series C, Growth either way; the entry date is the earlier of the two. Aligned with Redpoint's row (acquired, below_1b, Aliso Viejo).

Market cap $40.15B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis) replaces the prefilled October 2025 SEC float ($17.1B) as the public mark; same band as Sequoia's row (10b_plus, $39.0B on 2026-08-11). HQ San Jose. Public (Nasdaq: PACB, IPO October 2010); market cap $503.55M on 2026-09-25 at $1.62 a share (WallStreetZen). HQ Menlo Park. The firm listed PacBio from 2012 to 2017 (MD Jeff Bird) with its startup-era description, but no SEC filing names Sutter Hill with the company (EDGAR full-text search: zero hits) and Wikipedia's investor list (six rounds, nearly $400M) omits SHV, so SHV's round cannot be tied and the stage is undetermined. Membership rests on the listing alone; worth a look whether SHV's position began before the IPO (D4).

CA bought Nimsoft for $350M in March 2010 (Wikipedia; CA's 10-K for fiscal 2010 names the legal parent Nimsoft AS). The prefilled GB is a wrong join: Nimbus Software was founded in Oslo in 1998 and merged in 2004 with its US distributor, and the combined company's headquarters were established in Silicon Valley (Wikipedia); 2010 deal coverage places it in Redwood City. Total funding $22.3M (TechCrunch, 2010): the 2007 $10.3M Series A from JMI Equity and Northzone and the October 2008 $12M round led by Goldman Sachs. Neither names SHV, so its round is not on record and the stage is undetermined.

PMC-Sierra (fabless communications and storage chips) was acquired by Microsemi on January 15, 2016 (Wikipedia, PMC-Sierra). The prefilled GB is a wrong join: its last 10-K (February 2015) gives its principal offices in Sunnyvale, CA, with engineering in Burnaby, Canada. The firm's listing (2010 to 2016) is the only tie: no SEC filing names Sutter Hill with PMC-Sierra and no listed SHV company names PMC-Sierra as its acquirer, so no sale-consideration reading was found. SHV's entry round is not named in any record found, so the stage is undetermined.

Acquired by Honeywell in March 1997 for almost $600M (Wikipedia, Measurex); the firm's own 1999 table says 'Acquired by Honeywell'. So it reads acquired, aligned with Greylock's row (acquired, below_1b, Natick). SHV's entry round is not named in any record found, so the stage is undetermined.

SHV's entry round is not named in any record found, so the stage is undetermined.
